environment.description: Same Quarkus 3.2 serverless handler on AWS Lambda behind API Gateway (REST API type). Session cookies configured identically (SameSite=None; Secure; HttpOnly) for mobile compatibility. API Gateway has an associated AWS WAFv2 WebACL with a custom rule group 'csrf-origin-enforcement' that inspects the Origin and Referer headers on all POST/PUT/DELETE requests and blocks any request where neither header matches the pattern '^https://app\.example\.com($|/)'. Additionally, the settings.html Qute template references form-validation.js with a subresource integrity hash (sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC) and the response includes Content-Security-Policy: require-sri-for script; with script-src restricted to 'self' and the CDN origin. The SRI hash pins the exact script content, preventing any attacker-injected or CDN-compromised JavaScript from executing a forged form submission from within the legitimate page context. The WAF origin-check rule operates independently and blocks cross-origin state-changing requests at the network edge before they reach the Lambda function.

waf_custom_rule.name: csrf-origin-enforcement
waf_custom_rule.statement: ByteMatchStatement on Origin/Referer headers, negated match against '^https://app\.example\.com($|/)'
